+title: Render toolCalls/toolOutput transcript entries in TranscriptConverter and remove the Executor's single-turn tool-calling cap
+---
+## What
+NOTE: this work lives on the `origin/mlx-foundationmodels` branch (not `main`) — `main` has no `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/`. Base all work on `origin/mlx-foundationmodels`.
+
+**Verified problem (two coupled defects, one root cause):**
+
+1. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/TranscriptConverter.swift` — `mlxMessages(for:)`'s entry switch silently drops `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` transcript entries (`default: // Skip unsupported entry types (toolCalls, toolOutput, etc.)`). The model **never sees any tool result**: when `LanguageModelSession`'s auto-loop executes a tool and re-invokes the executor with the result appended, the converted prompt is identical to the previous round.
+2. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift` — `Executor.respond(to:model:streamingInto:)` has an explicit `isContinuationAfterToolCall` cap (comment: "Single-turn tool-calling cap … Multi-turn tool calling — where the model sees tool outputs in the transcript and continues with a data-aware response — is not supported."). Any continuation round skips the tool-grammar branch (gated on `!request.enabledToolDefinitions.isEmpty && !isContinuationAfterToolCall`) and falls through to **unconstrained plain text** — so the final answer is generated blind, without the tool's output. The cap exists only as a bandaid for defect 1 (re-entering the tool branch with an unchanged prompt would loop forever).
+
+**Provenance:** both defects shipped in the adapter's initial commit `134db41` ("Add MLXFoundationModels: an MLX-backed FoundationModels LanguageModel", ctymoszek, 2026-06-08) as a documented scope cut. No upstream issue exists — both `swissarmyhammer/mlx-swift-lm` and `ctymoszek/mlx-swift-lm` have GitHub issues disabled.
+
+**Prior art in this repo:** `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ChatSession.swift`'s own tool loop appends tool results as `Chat.Message.tool(toolResult)` (role `.tool`, `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Chat.swift`) and restarts generation with them in history — the tokenizer chat templates already render the tool role. The Executor's tool grammar (`SchemaConverter.encodeToolCallingGrammar` + synthetic `FinalAnswerTool`) already lets the model choose between calling a tool and answering, so re-entering the tool branch on continuation rounds needs no new grammar work.
+
+**Fix:**
+- [ ] In `TranscriptConverter.mlxMessages(for:)`, convert `.toolCalls` entries to an assistant `Chat.Message` carrying the tool-call envelope (name + arguments JSON, matching the `{"name": …, "arguments": …}` shape the Executor's own tool path emits) and `.toolOutput` entries to `Chat.Message.tool(…)` with the output segments' text — replacing the `default:` drop for these two cases (keep dropping genuinely unknown entry types).
+- [ ] In `Executor.respond`, remove the `isContinuationAfterToolCall` fall-through so continuation rounds re-enter the tool-grammar branch: the model sees prior tool calls + results in the prompt and chooses another tool call or the final answer. Delete or repurpose the two gates that reference it.
+- [ ] Update the stale doc comments that declare multi-turn tool calling unsupported (the cap comment block in `MLXLanguageModel.swift`, and any matching claim in `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/Documentation.docc/`).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `TranscriptConverter.mlxMessages(for:)` maps a transcript containing `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` entries to chat messages that include the tool call (assistant role) and the tool output (tool role) — no longer dropped.
+- [ ] A `LanguageModelSession(model: MLXLanguageModel(...), tools: [toolA, toolB])` can call `toolA`, receive its result, and then call `toolB` (or `toolA` again) in the same turn — the continuation round is constrained tool-grammar generation, not unconstrained text.
+- [ ] The final answer after a tool call is data-aware: a scripted tool returning a distinctive sentinel value produces a final response that reflects that sentinel (proves the model actually saw the tool output).
+- [ ] Single tool-call round-trip behavior is unchanged — existing `ToolCalling` suites pass without modification of their assertions.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Unit tests in `Tests/MLXFoundationModelsTests/TranscriptConverterTests.swift`: a transcript with `.toolCalls` → assistant message with the call envelope; `.toolOutput` → `.tool`-role message with the output text; ordering preserved relative to prompt/response entries.
+- [ ] Integration regression test in `IntegrationTesting/IntegrationTestingTests/MLXFoundationModelsIntegration/ToolCalling/` (extend `FoundationModelsToolCallingTests.swift` or add a multi-turn test file): two tools registered, first tool returns a sentinel; assert a second tool call occurs and/or the final answer contains the sentinel — this test fails against the current cap.
+- [ ] Existing suites pass: `Tests/MLXFoundationModelsTests` and `MLXFoundationModelsIntegration` (incl. `ToolCalling/ToolCallRoundTripTests.swift` and `Reasoning/`).
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the failing TranscriptConverter unit tests and the multi-turn integration test first, then implement the converter mapping and remove the cap.

This makes the control flow difficult to trace and reason about. Extract the tool-calling path (lines 938-1058), guided-generation path (lines 1059-1154), and text-generation dispatch (lines 1155-1162) into separate private methods: runToolCalling(), runGuidedGeneration(), and runTextGeneration(). This reduces the closure to a simple branch dispatcher and lowers maximum nesting depth from 5 to 3.
+- [ ] `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift:971` — The guided-generation setup block (lines 971–1007) is near-verbatim copied from the tool-calling path (lines 855–883). Both blocks perform identical steps: fetch xgTokenizer, create constraint, resolve maxTokens, compute bias and reserve values. They differ only in the `kind` parameter (.structuralTag vs .json) and schemaJSON source (toolCallingEnvelopeJSON vs schemaJSON). -## What
-NOTE: this work lives on the `origin/mlx-foundationmodels` branch (not `main`) — `main` has no `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/`. Base all work on `origin/mlx-foundationmodels`.
-
-**Verified problem (two coupled defects, one root cause):**
-
-1. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/TranscriptConverter.swift` — `mlxMessages(for:)`'s entry switch silently drops `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` transcript entries (`default: // Skip unsupported entry types (toolCalls, toolOutput, etc.)`). The model **never sees any tool result**: when `LanguageModelSession`'s auto-loop executes a tool and re-invokes the executor with the result appended, the converted prompt is identical to the previous round.
-2. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift` — `Executor.respond(to:model:streamingInto:)` has an explicit `isContinuationAfterToolCall` cap (comment: "Single-turn tool-calling cap … Multi-turn tool calling — where the model sees tool outputs in the transcript and continues with a data-aware response — is not supported."). Any continuation round skips the tool-grammar branch (gated on `!request.enabledToolDefinitions.isEmpty && !isContinuationAfterToolCall`) and falls through to **unconstrained plain text** — so the final answer is generated blind, without the tool's output. The cap exists only as a bandaid for defect 1 (re-entering the tool branch with an unchanged prompt would loop forever).
-
-**Provenance:** both defects shipped in the adapter's initial commit `134db41` ("Add MLXFoundationModels: an MLX-backed FoundationModels LanguageModel", ctymoszek, 2026-06-08) as a documented scope cut. No upstream issue exists — both `swissarmyhammer/mlx-swift-lm` and `ctymoszek/mlx-swift-lm` have GitHub issues disabled.
-
-**Prior art in this repo:** `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ChatSession.swift`'s own tool loop appends tool results as `Chat.Message.tool(toolResult)` (role `.tool`, `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Chat.swift`) and restarts generation with them in history — the tokenizer chat templates already render the tool role. The Executor's tool grammar (`SchemaConverter.encodeToolCallingGrammar` + synthetic `FinalAnswerTool`) already lets the model choose between calling a tool and answering, so re-entering the tool branch on continuation rounds needs no new grammar work.
-
-**Fix:**
-- [x] In `TranscriptConverter.mlxMessages(for:)`, convert `.toolCalls` entries to an assistant `Chat.Message` carrying the tool-call envelope (name + arguments JSON, matching the `{"name": …, "arguments": …}` shape the Executor's own tool path emits) and `.toolOutput` entries to `Chat.Message.tool(…)` with the output segments' text — replacing the `default:` drop for these two cases (keep dropping genuinely unknown entry types).
-- [x] In `Executor.respond`, remove the `isContinuationAfterToolCall` fall-through so continuation rounds re-enter the tool-grammar branch: the model sees prior tool calls + results in the prompt and chooses another tool call or the final answer. Delete or repurpose the two gates that reference it.
-- [x] Update the stale doc comments that declare multi-turn tool calling unsupported (the cap comment block in `MLXLanguageModel.swift`, and any matching claim in `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/Documentation.docc/` — verified: docc has no such claim; it lived only in the removed comment block).
-
-## Acceptance Criteria
-- [x] `TranscriptConverter.mlxMessages(for:)` maps a transcript containing `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` entries to chat messages that include the tool call (assistant role) and the tool output (tool role) — no longer dropped. (Unit-verified: 20/20 TranscriptConverterTests pass.)
-- [x] A `LanguageModelSession(model: MLXLanguageModel(...), tools: [toolA, toolB])` can call `toolA`, receive its result, and then call `toolB` (or `toolA` again) in the same turn — the continuation round is constrained tool-grammar generation, not unconstrained text. -- [x] The final answer after a tool call is data-aware: a scripted tool returning a distinctive sentinel value produces a final response that reflects that sentinel (proves the model actually saw the tool output). (Live-verified in the same run — `toolOutputSentinelReachesFinalAnswer()` passed.)
-- [x] Single tool-call round-trip behavior is unchanged — existing `ToolCalling` suites pass without modification of their assertions. (Assertions untouched; first-round code path identical; full `MLXFoundationModelsTests` 83/83 pass, zero warnings.)
-

-- [x] Integration regression test in `IntegrationTesting/IntegrationTestingTests/MLXFoundationModelsIntegration/ToolCalling/` (`MultiTurnToolCallingTests.swift`): two tools registered, first tool returns a sentinel; asserts a second-round data-aware final answer contains the sentinel — this test fails against the old cap. Extract the token processing logic (lines 1285-1295) into a separate helper method processTokenForReasoning(_ token, _ emitter, _ detokenizer) that returns the segment sequence. This reduces nesting by one level and simplifies the main loop to: for await generation in generateTokens(...) { switch generation { case .token(let token): for segment in try processTokenForReasoning(token, &emitter, &detokenizer) { await Self.send(...) } ...
-- [x] `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/TranscriptConverter.swift:128` — extractToolOutputText reimplements nearly identical logic to extractText instead of generalizing into one function. Both filter segments, extract text, join with newlines, and log skipped segments; the only differences are that extractToolOutputText also handles .structure segments and returns empty string vs nil. Refactor to a single generalized function with parameters controlling whether to include structure segments and what to return for empty content, or have extractToolOutputText call extractText with additional logic for structure cases.

-## What
NOTE: this work lives on the `origin/mlx-foundationmodels` branch (not `main`) — `main` has no `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/`. Base all work on `origin/mlx-foundationmodels`.

**Verified problem (two coupled defects, one root cause):**

1. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/TranscriptConverter.swift` — `mlxMessages(for:)`'s entry switch silently drops `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` transcript entries (`default: // Skip unsupported entry types (toolCalls, toolOutput, etc.)`). The model **never sees any tool result**: when `LanguageModelSession`'s auto-loop executes a tool and re-invokes the executor with the result appended, the converted prompt is identical to the previous round.
2. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift` — `Executor.respond(to:model:streamingInto:)` has an explicit `isContinuationAfterToolCall` cap (comment: "Single-turn tool-calling cap … Multi-turn tool calling — where the model sees tool outputs in the transcript and continues with a data-aware response — is not supported."). Any continuation round skips the tool-grammar branch (gated on `!request.enabledToolDefinitions.isEmpty && !isContinuationAfterToolCall`) and falls through to **unconstrained plain text** — so the final answer is generated blind, without the tool's output. The cap exists only as a bandaid for defect 1 (re-entering the tool branch with an unchanged prompt would loop forever).

**Provenance:** both defects shipped in the adapter's initial commit `134db41` ("Add MLXFoundationModels: an MLX-backed FoundationModels LanguageModel", ctymoszek, 2026-06-08) as a documented scope cut. No upstream issue exists — both `swissarmyhammer/mlx-swift-lm` and `ctymoszek/mlx-swift-lm` have GitHub issues disabled.

**Prior art in this repo:** `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ChatSession.swift`'s own tool loop appends tool results as `Chat.Message.tool(toolResult)` (role `.tool`, `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Chat.swift`) and restarts generation with them in history — the tokenizer chat templates already render the tool role. The Executor's tool grammar (`SchemaConverter.encodeToolCallingGrammar` + synthetic `FinalAnswerTool`) already lets the model choose between calling a tool and answering, so re-entering the tool branch on continuation rounds needs no new grammar work.

**Fix:**
- [x] In `TranscriptConverter.mlxMessages(for:)`, convert `.toolCalls` entries to an assistant `Chat.Message` carrying the tool-call envelope (name + arguments JSON, matching the `{"name": …, "arguments": …}` shape the Executor's own tool path emits) and `.toolOutput` entries to `Chat.Message.tool(…)` with the output segments' text — replacing the `default:` drop for these two cases (keep dropping genuinely unknown entry types).
- [x] In `Executor.respond`, remove the `isContinuationAfterToolCall` fall-through so continuation rounds re-enter the tool-grammar branch: the model sees prior tool calls + results in the prompt and chooses another tool call or the final answer. Delete or repurpose the two gates that reference it.
- [x] Update the stale doc comments that declare multi-turn tool calling unsupported (the cap comment block in `MLXLanguageModel.swift`, and any matching claim in `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/Documentation.docc/` — verified: docc has no such claim; it lived only in the removed comment block).

- [x] A `LanguageModelSession(model: MLXLanguageModel(...), tools: [toolA, toolB])` can call `toolA`, receive its result, and then call `toolB` (or `toolA` again) in the same turn — the continuation round is constrained tool-grammar generation, not unconstrained text. -**Verified problem (two coupled defects, one root cause):**

-1. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/TranscriptConverter.swift` — `mlxMessages(for:)`'s entry switch silently drops `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` transcript entries (`default: // Skip unsupported entry types (toolCalls, toolOutput, etc.)`). -2. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift` — `Executor.respond(to:model:streamingInto:)` has an explicit `isContinuationAfterToolCall` cap (comment: "Single-turn tool-calling cap … Multi-turn tool calling — where the model sees tool outputs in the transcript and continues with a data-aware response — is not supported."). Any continuation round skips the tool-grammar branch (gated on `!request.enabledToolDefinitions.isEmpty && !isContinuationAfterToolCall`) and falls through to **unconstrained plain text** — so the final answer is generated blind, without the tool's output. The cap exists only as a bandaid for defect 1 (re-entering the tool branch with an unchanged prompt would loop forever).
-
-**Provenance:** both defects shipped in the adapter's initial commit `134db41` ("Add MLXFoundationModels: an MLX-backed FoundationModels LanguageModel", ctymoszek, 2026-06-08) as a documented scope cut. No upstream issue exists — both `swissarmyhammer/mlx-swift-lm` and `ctymoszek/mlx-swift-lm` have GitHub issues disabled.
-
-**Prior art in this repo:** `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ChatSession.swift`'s own tool loop appends tool results as `Chat.Message.tool(toolResult)` (role `.tool`, `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Chat.swift`) and restarts generation with them in history — the tokenizer chat templates already render the tool role. The Executor's tool grammar (`SchemaConverter.encodeToolCallingGrammar` + synthetic `FinalAnswerTool`) already lets the model choose between calling a tool and answering, so re-entering the tool branch on continuation rounds needs no new grammar work.

-- [x] In `TranscriptConverter.mlxMessages(for:)`, convert `.toolCalls` entries to an assistant `Chat.Message` carrying the tool-call envelope (name + arguments JSON, matching the `{"name": …, "arguments": …}` shape the Executor's own tool path emits) and `.toolOutput` entries to `Chat.Message.tool(…)` with the output segments' text — replacing the `default:` drop for these two cases (keep dropping genuinely unknown entry types).
-- [x] In `Executor.respond`, remove the `isContinuationAfterToolCall` fall-through so continuation rounds re-enter the tool-grammar branch: the model sees prior tool calls + results in the prompt and chooses another tool call or the final answer. Delete or repurpose the two gates that reference it.
-- [x] Update the stale doc comments that declare multi-turn tool calling unsupported (the cap comment block in `MLXLanguageModel.swift`, and any matching claim in `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/Documentation.docc/` — verified: docc has no such claim; it lived only in the removed comment block).

-
-**Verified problem (two coupled defects, one root cause):**
-
-1. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/TranscriptConverter.swift` — `mlxMessages(for:)`'s entry switch silently drops `.toolCalls` and `.toolOutput` transcript entries (`default: // Skip unsupported entry types (toolCalls, toolOutput, etc.)`). The model **never sees any tool result**: when `LanguageModelSession`'s auto-loop executes a tool and re-invokes the executor with the result appended, the converted prompt is identical to the previous round.
-2. `Libraries/MLXFoundationModels/MLXLanguageModel.swift` — `Executor.respond(to:model:streamingInto:)` has an explicit `isContinuationAfterToolCall` cap (comment: "Single-turn tool-calling cap … Multi-turn tool calling — where the model sees tool outputs in the transcript and continues with a data-aware response — is not supported."). Any continuation round skips the tool-grammar branch (gated on `!request.enabledToolDefinitions.isEmpty && !isContinuationAfterToolCall`) and falls through to **unconstrained plain text** — so the final answer is generated blind, without the tool's output. The cap exists only as a bandaid for defect 1 (re-entering the tool branch with an unchanged prompt would loop forever).
-
-**Provenance:** both defects shipped in the adapter's initial commit `134db41` ("Add MLXFoundationModels: an MLX-backed FoundationModels LanguageModel", ctymoszek, 2026-06-08) as a documented scope cut. No upstream issue exists — both `swissarmyhammer/mlx-swift-lm` and `ctymoszek/mlx-swift-lm` have GitHub issues disabled.
-
-**Prior art in this repo:** `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/ChatSession.swift`'s own tool loop appends tool results as `Chat.Message.tool(toolResult)` (role `.tool`, `Libraries/MLXLMCommon/Chat.swift`) and restarts generation with them in history — the tokenizer chat templates already render the tool role. The Executor's tool grammar (`SchemaConverter.encodeToolCallingGrammar` + synthetic `FinalAnswerTool`) already lets the model choose between calling a tool and answering, so re-entering the tool branch on continuation rounds needs no new grammar work.

-- [x] In `Executor.respond`, remove the `isContinuationAfterToolCall` fall-through so continuation rounds re-enter the tool-grammar branch: the model sees prior tool calls + results in the prompt and chooses another tool call or the final answer. Delete or repurpose the two gates that reference it.
